## Project rules for coding agents (chipgraph)

These rules come from this repository's chipgraph profile and the organization rules it
extends. Follow them whenever you add or change a file.

### Project and blocks

- Project: `demo`
- Extends: `org:qnsc`
- Packs: `spec_core`
- Chip spec: `chip.yml` (format `chip-yaml`)
- Per-IP specs: `doc/ip`
- Target: asic, PDK `gf180mcu`

Each block is an IP. Its instances are the names the chip's memory map uses for it; a
block with no instances listed matches the instance of the same name.

| Block | Instances |
|---|---|
| `rom` | - |
| `top` | - |
| `uart` | `uart_0`, `uart_1` |

### Where files go

Create each kind of file only at the path its template gives; do not invent new
directories. In a template, `{block}` is the block name.

| Kind | Path template |
|---|---|
| filelist | `design/{block}/{block}.f` |
| generated | `design/top/rtl/demo_pkg.sv`, `doc/specs/docx/**` |
| rtl | `design/{block}/rtl/{module}.sv` |
| vendor | `vendor/**` |

Per-block overrides:

| Block | Kind | Path template |
|---|---|---|
| `rom` | spec | `doc/specs/ROM_MAS.md`, `doc/specs/BOOT.md` |

### Naming

From `org:qnsc/naming-v1.yml` (QNSC_RTL_Design_Naming_Rule v1.1). The whole
name must match the pattern for its kind:

| Kind | Pattern | Rule | Message |
|---|---|---|---|
| module | `^(?:m_qnsc_wrap_[a-z0-9_]+\|m_qnsc_[a-z0-9_]+\|qnsc_[a-z0-9_]+)$` | 2.1 module | must be m_qnsc_\<function>, m_qnsc_wrap_\<block> or qnsc_\<function> |
| port | `^(?:i_\|o_\|io_)[a-z0-9_]+$` | 1.2 port prefix | must start with i_, o_ or io_ |
| parameter | `^(?:P_\|C_\|S_)[A-Z0-9_]+$` | 2.4 parameter | must be P_\<FUNCTION> (parameter), C_\<FUNCTION> (constant) or S_\<STATE> (FSM state), uppercase |
| localparam | `^(?:P_\|C_\|S_)[A-Z0-9_]+$` | 2.4 parameter | must be P_\<FUNCTION> (parameter), C_\<FUNCTION> (constant) or S_\<STATE> (FSM state), uppercase |
| enum_value | `^S_[A-Z0-9_]+$` | 2.4 parameter | an FSM state must be S_\<STATE>, uppercase |
| instance | `^u_[a-z0-9_]+$` | 2.2 instance | must be u_\<function>[_\<index>] |
| signal | `^(?:r_\|w_\|mem_)[a-z0-9_]+$` | 2.3 signal | must be r_\<function> if registered, w_\<function> if combinational, or mem_\<function> if a memory array |
| memory | `^mem_[a-z0-9_]+$` | 2.3 signal | a memory array must be mem_\<function> |
| genvar | `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$` | 2.3 signal | must be lowercase with _ only |

Every declared name also follows:

- 1.1 case: uses mixed case; identifiers are lowercase with _ (uppercase only for P_/C_/S_)
- 1.3 active low: active low is _n after the meaning, as in i_rst_n_sys
- 1.4 index: a numeric index takes an underscore, as in timer_0

Words (1.5 vocabulary): use the project term on the right, never the
word on the left: `analog` -> `ana`, `clock` -> `clk`, `config` -> `cfg`, `debug` -> `dbg`, `interrupt` -> `int`, `irq` -> `int`, `memory` -> `mem`, `multiplexer` -> `mux`, `peripheral` -> `peri`, `power` -> `pwr`, `reset` -> `rst`.

A declaration line that ends with the comment `naming-check: ignore` is exempt;
use it only with a reason the reviewer accepts.

### Before you open a PR

Run these from the repository root and fix what they report:

```sh
chipgraph ingest    # build the Design Model; the cross checks read it
chipgraph check     # run every configured check; exits 1 if one fails
chipgraph audit     # every finding, grouped by layer
```

Scope a run with `chipgraph check --block <block>` or `chipgraph check --only <check>`.
`chipgraph ingest --strict` and `chipgraph audit --strict` also exit 1, on an error-level
ingest issue or a blocking finding.

Configured checks (a severity caps what the check reports; a command's `{block}` is the
block name):

| Check | Adapter | Severity | Command |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lint` | cmd | - | `make lint BLOCK={block}` |
| `naming` | naming | - | - |
| `regs` | generated | - | - |
| `trace` | trace | warning | - |

Per-block check overrides:

| Block | Check | Adapter | Severity | Command |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `uart` | `lint` | cmd | info | `make lint-uart` |

### Requirement IDs

- A requirement ID in a spec must match `REQ-{BLOCK}-\d+`, with `{block}`/`{BLOCK}` replaced by the block name in lower/upper case (for `top`: `REQ-TOP-\d+`).
- Name the ID in the test that covers it: the `trace` check traces each requirement to a test.

Per-block overrides:

| Block | ID pattern | Inferred from "Verification" |
|---|---|---|
| `rom` | `(?:ROM\|BOOT)_\d{3}` | yes |

### Path exceptions

These paths follow different rules. Do not write under a path whose write is `deny`,
and do not add a new exception without a reason the reviewer accepts.

| Path | Block | Checks | Write | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `hw/legacy/**` | - | naming off | allow | old code from chip v1 \| kept as is |
| `vendor/**` | - | header off, naming off | deny | vendor IP |
| `design/uart/rtl/old/**` | `uart` | - | deny | frozen \<v1> RTL |

### Data labels

Files matching these paths are labeled `nda`. Never send their content to a cloud model
(do not paste it into a prompt, an issue or a web tool); only a local model may read them (`nda_model: local`).

- `doc/nda/**`
- `vendor/pdk/**`

### Generated files

chipgraph or the project's flow generates these files. Do not edit them by hand: change
their source and regenerate them.

- `design/*/rtl/*_regs.sv`
- `design/top/rtl/demo_pkg.sv`
- `doc/specs/docx/**`
